findings.finding: The "path absent" arm relies on the claim that `git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>` "needs only trees". `cat-file -e` checks that the resolved object exists, and in this case that object is the blob. In the blobless clone the plan itself creates, a blob that is missing and cannot be lazily fetched makes `cat-file -e` fail. The plan routes that failure to "fall through to the next candidate, then to an empty project layer", even though its second arm says an unfetchable blob should be a `ConfigError`. An empty project layer drops main's `require_environment`, and the gate then exits 0 in advisory mode. That is fail-open. A tree-only existence check, such as `git ls-tree <ref> -- <path>` or `git rev-parse --verify -q <ref>:<path>`, would actually need only trees.
findings.location: Approach: failure-handling arm "the path is absent at the ref (`git cat-file -e` fails, which needs only trees)"

findings.finding: The plan says checking a path with `git cat-file -e` 'needs only trees'. In a partial (blobless) clone that is false. `cat-file -e <ref>:<path>` checks whether the blob exists and, if it is missing, starts a lazy promisor fetch. If that fetch fails, the command fails the same way it does for a missing path. In the CI checkout (blobless), a main `rebar.toml` that cannot be fetched would therefore be classed as 'absent'. The gate would fall through to `pyproject.toml` or an empty project layer and drop main's `require_environment`, so it fails open. The separate arm 'git show of a present path fails (for example a blobless clone cannot fetch the blob) → ConfigError' can then never run, because the presence check has already hidden that case.
findings.location: Approach → Failure handling, 'the path is absent at the ref (`git cat-file -e` fails, which needs only trees)'
scenarios: The CI runner's lazy fetch of main's `rebar.toml` blob fails (transient network or auth error, or the promisor is unreachable). `cat-file -e` exits non-zero, the gate treats `rebar.toml` as absent, uses the empty project layer, and drops `verify.require_environment`, so the gate runs looser than main intends.

findings.finding: The plan says the 'path is absent at the ref' check, `git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>`, 'needs only trees'. It doesn't. `cat-file -e` checks that the resolved object (the blob) exists. In a blobless partial clone it fetches the blob on demand, and if that fetch fails it exits non-zero, exactly as it would for a missing path. So the 'blobless clone cannot fetch the blob' arm, which the plan says must raise ConfigError and exit 2, instead lands in the 'absent → fall through to the next candidate, then to an empty project layer' arm. The gate then runs on the next candidate or on an empty project layer: it fails open, which is the opposite of the failure handling the plan specifies.

findings.finding: The base ref is hardcoded to `refs/remotes/origin/main`, and 'a remote exists but origin/main does not resolve' is a hard ConfigError (exit 2). Any project whose reviewed branch is not literally `main` on a remote named `origin` can therefore never run `rebar verify-opcert` successfully. That includes projects on `master`/`trunk`/`develop`, or with only an `upstream` remote. The plan also forbids any key or flag to change the ref, so such projects have no recourse.
findings.location: Approach — 'Base ref: `refs/remotes/origin/main` only' / 'No config key, env var or flag is added: the base ref is fixed at `origin/main`.'
scenarios: Target project whose default branch is `master`, on GitLab CI or a developer workstation: `origin/main` never exists. Every `rebar verify-opcert` run exits 2 telling the user to `git fetch origin`, which cannot fix it.
Fork workflow with only an `upstream` remote: `git remote` is non-empty but `origin/main` is absent, so the gate exits 2 permanently.
A PR targeting a release branch: the gate silently uses main's trust list instead of the branch it merges into.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the base from `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` when present, falling back to `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Have the CI step fetch the PR's base ref (e.g. `${{ github.base_ref }}`) into that ref. Keep exit 2 only when no candidate resolves.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the reuse of `rebar._snapshot.git_fetch.has_remote`, `rev_parse` and `git_run` (and their SnapshotError-on-timeout behaviour, mapped to ConfigError/exit 2) for the no-remote / unresolved-`origin/main` / `cat-file -e` / `git show` arms instead of new git subprocess calls.
evidence: Plan: "no remote at all (`git remote` prints nothing): no reviewed branch and no change under review, so the working-tree configuration is kept."
src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py:131-137 `has_remote`: "raises :class:`SnapshotError` if `git remote` times out rather than answering \"absent\""
src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py:140-155 `rev_parse`: "A timed-out `git rev-parse` raises ... so it is never reported as an unresolvable ref"

findings.finding: The failure-handling arms describe their own git checks: `git remote` printing nothing to mean "no remote", resolving `origin/main`, and `git cat-file -e` for path presence. The repo already has timeout-bounded, fail-closed helpers for exactly the first two: `has_remote` (git_fetch.py:131), which raises SnapshotError on a watchdog timeout instead of reporting "absent", `rev_parse` (git_fetch.py:140), which uses `--verify --quiet --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}` and raises on timeout, and the generic bounded `git_run`. The plan names none of them. A hand-rolled `git remote` that treats empty or timed-out output as "no remote" lands in the "working-tree configuration is kept" arm. That is a fail-open path the existing helper was written to prevent.
findings.location: Approach — "Failure handling, every arm" sub-bullets
scenarios: On a loaded CI runner a slow `git remote` is killed by a watchdog and returns empty stdout. A new implementation that reads this as "prints nothing" falls back to the working-tree `rebar.toml`, which is the very trust-widening the plan is meant to close.
A ref that names a non-commit object resolves under a bare `git rev-parse origin/main` but not under the existing `^{commit}`-pinned helper, so the two paths disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: In `_opcert_gate_config`: `if not has_remote(root, "origin")` → keep working-tree config; `sha = rev_parse(root, DEFAULT_REF)` → `None` raises ConfigError naming `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main`; run `cat-file -e <sha>:<path>` and `show <sha>:<path>` through `git_run` (with `_raise_if_timed_out`). Convert any SnapshotError into ConfigError so a timeout exits 2 rather than falling back to the working tree.

CI systems that fetch a commit by URL or SHA without creating a named remote, or that build from a `git init` workspace, also produce zero remotes. There the gate reads the change's own `rebar.toml`, and the only signal is a stderr line.

findings.location: Testing — 'Existing tests/unit/test_verify_opcert.py and tests/unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py … pass unchanged'; last Acceptance Criterion pytest command
scenarios: A regression in the no-remote fallback or the env-layer merge inside `gate_config` breaks this suite. The targeted AC command still passes, and the break shows up only in the full `make verify`.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the last AC to: `pytest tests/unit/test_opcert_gate_config.py tests/unit/test_verify_opcert.py tests/unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py tests/unit/test_mcp_opcert_signing_goose.py` passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the default: per-directory precedence identical to `_discover_project_config` (rebar.toml, then pyproject.toml [tool.rebar], then move up), with a test covering the nested case.
evidence: "It walks from the project root up to the git top level and takes the nearest `rebar.toml`, else a `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.rebar]`."
findings.finding: The discovery precedence at the ref is ambiguous. 'takes the nearest rebar.toml, else a pyproject.toml with [tool.rebar]' can mean two things: a nearest rebar.toml at any level beats a closer pyproject, or per directory rebar.toml then pyproject before moving up. It is also not stated whether this must mirror `_discover_project_config`'s semantics.
findings.location: Approach, first bullet (walk rule)
scenarios: A monorepo has a pyproject.toml [tool.rebar] in the package directory and a rebar.toml at the top level; the gate picks a different file than normal config loading does.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the arm for 'not a git repository / git not installed' (default: treat as no remote and keep the working-tree config) and add a test for it.
evidence: "no remote at all (`git remote` prints nothing): ... the working-tree configuration is kept."
"Existing tests/unit/test_verify_opcert.py and tests/unit/test_verify_opcert_ac_coverage.py (remote-less fixtures) pass unchanged."
findings.finding: The plan does not say what happens when `--root` is not inside a git repository, or when git is unavailable. `git remote` then exits non-zero (e.g. 128) rather than 'printing nothing', and neither the fail-closed arm nor the working-tree arm is chosen explicitly. This matters because the plan requires the existing remote-less fixtures to pass unchanged, and those may be plain temp directories with no `git init`.
findings.location: Approach > Failure handling, 'no remote at all' arm; Testing > existing test_verify_opcert.py fixtures
scenarios: A fixture tmpdir is not a git repo; the implementer either raises ConfigError and breaks the existing tests, or treats it as no-remote without deciding that this is intended.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fifth failure arm: if `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails, return the working-tree configuration with source 'working tree (not a git checkout)', and print it to stderr like the other sources.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Build `gate_config` by injecting a project-layer source into the existing `raw_layers` → `_ordered_layers` → `_compose` → `compose_operation_snapshot` path instead of re-composing user/env/cli layers in a new module.
evidence: Plan: "It composes the same labelled layers as `load_config` (`src/rebar/config.py:468` `_compose`) — user config, project, env overrides, process `-c` overrides — but the project layer is the project config committed at the base ref"
src/rebar/_config_sources.py:201 `raw_layers(root)` is "The single discovery walk every raw-config reader shares"
src/rebar/config.py:349-368 `_ordered_layers` builds user/project/env/cli layers from `raw_layers` and applies `coerce_sparse(..., strict=strict)`
src/rebar/config.py:468-480 `_compose` is "The single composition `load_config` and `resolve_with_sources` share, so displayed provenance always matches resolved values"
src/rebar/_operation_config.py:165-185 `compose_operation_snapshot` already builds an OperationSnapshot from `resolve_with_sources`
findings.finding: `gate_config` is specified to compose "the same labelled layers as `load_config`" (user, project, env, process `-c` overrides) in a new module, and then to build an OperationSnapshot from the result. That rebuilds code the repo already shares in one place: `raw_layers` (_config_sources.py:201) yields user+project, `_ordered_layers` (config.py:349) adds env/cli with `coerce_sparse(..., strict=_strict_unknown_keys())`, `_compose` (config.py:468) merges and derives per-key provenance via `_winning_label`, and `compose_operation_snapshot` (_operation_config.py:165) turns that into the snapshot. Only the project-layer source differs. A second copy can drift from the first: strict/unknown-key policy, `env_overrides` coercion, provenance labels that `OperationSnapshot.build` checks against `_source_kinds()`, and the retired-file/env tombstone checks `load_config` runs (config.py:494-501).
findings.location: Approach — first bullet (`src/rebar/_opcert_gate_config.py` / `gate_config(root)`)
scenarios: A later change to `_ordered_layers` (for example a new layer, a change to strict-key policy, or tombstone handling) reaches `rebar verify-opcert` everywhere except the gate, so the gate quietly resolves config differently from every other command.
A provenance label `gate_config` produces that is not in `_source_kinds()` makes `OperationSnapshot.build` raise ValueError at gate time.
findings.suggested_fix: Give `raw_layers`/`_ordered_layers` (and through them `resolve_with_sources` / `compose_operation_snapshot`) an optional `project_layer` argument, e.g. a pre-read `RawLayer` or a callable returning `(label_path, kind, raw) | None`, that replaces `_discover_project_config` when supplied. `_opcert_gate_config` then only implements "read the nearest rebar.toml / [tool.rebar] pyproject at origin/main via git" and passes it in. It reuses the existing user/env/cli layering, coercion, provenance and snapshot construction unchanged.
